_comment: The golden set. Five synthetic transcripts for fictional shows - no copyrighted
material, nothing scraped. Each case is chosen to stress a different failure mode
of the summarisation prompt, not to be representative of an 'average' episode.
target_minutes feeds the length-adherence metric via the 150 words-per-minute

cases.stresses: Baseline. Short, clean, two speakers, one clear escalating plot line.
cases.expect: Everything should pass here. A regression on this case is a real regression.

cases.stresses: Thirty short exchanges, three speakers, argument-shaped. Plot is implied by dialogue rather than stated.
cases.expect: Grounding is the risk: models tend to summarise the mood and drop the named characters.

cases.stresses: The interesting failure case. A scrape that succeeded structurally and returned nothing usable.
cases.expect: Either an honest refusal or a hallucinated episode. The eval does not score a refusal as success; it scores whether the output is empty (output_present) and whether anything it says is grounded. A confident, fluent, entirely invented summary should score WORSE here than a short honest one.

cases.stresses: Timestamps, HTML entities, ALL-CAPS shouting, inconsistent speaker markers, scene-break sigils, lowercase dialogue.
cases.expect: Entity extraction has to survive the noise, and the model has to not echo the formatting into the narration script.

cases.stresses: Five named speakers plus a narrator, a technical premise, and a consequence that lands outside the episode.
cases.expect: Coverage is the risk: the minor characters (Vesper, Halden) are the ones that get dropped first.
